log.after: The Stakeholder Insights Report mapped all 223 of its insight statements to tree entries before aggregating them (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p5, p20 to p46). Because the study team mapped the insights to tree entries, the counts show where views cluster; they do not on their own validate an entry.

**What the evidence argued against.** No entry was withdrawn, but the evidence narrowed or overturned three parts of the December case. First, the pivot to four growth markets narrowed to converting India and China traffic already flying through hubs; the Middle East and ASEAN cases did not survive (focus area 4). Second, the ambition to double arrivals did not survive: the growth model supports 2.2 million to 2.5 million by 2035 (section 1.1). Third, the 300,000 tourism-linked jobs ambition has no baseline behind it and is flagged untested (focus area 20). Two Validated entries also rest on less than direct evidence: focus area 5 has no fare or yield data, and focus area 15 is an inference from the pipeline tables (section 3.3).

log.before: The Western Cape can grow international arrivals from about 1.5 million in 2025 to between 2.2 million and 2.5 million by 2035. Supply, not demand, sets the pace. || Wesgro commissioned an evidence-based strategy to double international tourist arrivals to the Western Cape by 2035 (Inception Report, Nov 2025, p4). The study tested an eighteen-entry hypothesis tree against seven deliverables and four working analyses between December 2025 and October 2026. This report sets out what the evidence found, what Wesgro and its partners should do and how progress will be measured. || The evidence reframes the ambition as growth to 2.5 million arrivals, set by supply rather than demand. From 1,498,829 arrivals in 2025 the growth model reaches 2,175,778 on the base path and 2,516,282 on the accelerated path in 2035 (Market Assessment Report, May 2026, p19; Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026, p20). International passenger arrivals at Cape Town International, the series ACSA reports, stood at 1.44m in FY24/25 and 1.57m in FY25/26 (Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026, p11).
log.after: The Western Cape can grow international arrivals from about 1.5 million in 2025 to 2.2 million by 2035 on the base path, and to 2.5 million on the accelerated path. Gateway capacity sets the pace in the summer peak; demand and conversion set it in the green season and beyond the Metro. || From 1,498,829 arrivals in 2025 the growth model reaches 2,175,778 on the base path and 2,516,282 on the accelerated path in 2035 (Market Assessment Report, May 2026, p19; Demand-Side Analysis, Jun 2026, p20).
